paraphrase: You give birth to the world, protect it and at dissolution withdraw it — so you are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa; many serve other gods, deluded, not knowing the supreme; I take refuge in the primal one worshipped by Hari, Hara and Brahmā; earth, water, fire, wind and sky — you alone, auspicious Kālī, beloved of Śiva, are all; be gracious, that I be born no more.

paraphrase: What shall we say of you, Mother, dull-witted as we are? Neither Brahmā nor Śiva nor even Hari knows your supreme nature; yet devotion to you makes us speak — forgive it; anger at a mere beast (paśu) is not fitting.
